verdict.answer_key: PASS: no material factual contradiction or requested-answer omission established in Q01–Q60.
verdict.reason: Two explicit base rules are not directly challenged: the own-turn-only window for special actions, and mandatory collection of ordinary non-optional positive favours. Each changes a legal decision; neither requires expansion content or a numeric/cosmetic variation.
verdict.qualification: Coverage verdict applies to direct rule testing in this question bank. It does not assert that every unasked tile value or objective recipe needs its own question.

proposed_meaningful_additions.question: While another player is taking their turn, may you spend reputation to Borrow Money, use Service Help, or refresh the Market as an interrupt? During which part of your own turn may you take these actions?
proposed_meaningful_additions.expected_answer: No: special actions may be taken only during your own turn. They may be taken at any time during that turn, when hosting or passing, subject to their individual costs and limits, including in the middle of resolving a favour.
proposed_meaningful_additions.distinct_rule: Legal timing window and prohibition on out-of-turn interruption; affects whether a player can alter an opponent’s Market or reputation-linked decisions.
proposed_meaningful_additions.why_not_duplicate: Q06 asks costs, repetitions and minimum restrictions; Q34 asks avoiding wasted maximum reputation; Q60 separates refresh methods. None asks whether any special action may interrupt another player. Q34 already covers flexibility within favours, so the new material is the own-turn boundary.

proposed_meaningful_additions.question: An ordinary activity gives you a casual-guest invite, but you would rather not risk drawing an unwanted guest. May you decline that printed invite while enjoying the other favours? How does an optional dismissal favour differ?
proposed_meaningful_additions.expected_answer: No. Printed favours are mandatory unless they use an optional term such as may. Resolve the ordinary invite and reveal/add the drawn guest; you cannot skip it merely because it may be undesirable. A dismissal favour is optional and may be declined.
proposed_meaningful_additions.distinct_rule: Mandatory collection of an ordinary positive favour versus player discretion; determines whether a guest draw can be refused.
proposed_meaningful_additions.why_not_duplicate: Q05 covers order and mandatory negative payments; Q37 covers disclosure and destinations once inviting/screening; Q38 covers optional dismissal. None explicitly tests refusal of a non-optional positive favour.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Add every unasked base objective group or fixed tile/servant threshold
rejected_candidates.reason: Different tile names or required numbers do not introduce a new completion rule. Q16 covers possession without upgrade and Q51–Q55 cover the substantive counting exceptions.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Newly bought monument does not award reputation immediately
rejected_candidates.reason: Follows the existing event/ongoing-before-activity-before-buy sequence in Q02/Q19. No separate source-defined acquisition exception.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Newly drawn guest cannot join the activity whose favour drew it
rejected_candidates.reason: Recombines Q02 invitation/favour timing and Q37 destination, without a distinct exception.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Dismiss a currently attending guest to evade its later negative favour
rejected_candidates.reason: All played gentry contribute favours, and positive-before-negative is already tested in Q05 while Q38 tests activity dismissal. No explicit source exception that changes those rules; do not manufacture one.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Interleave special-action spending with oversized reputation reward
